title: The empty place, the reshimu and the Kav: G-d hides Himself so that the work is ours
overview:
Chapter 13 is the *nimshal* of chapter 12's analogies. The *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* is G-d hiding His essential light so that something that seems separate from Him can exist. But like the teacher who teaches in short, He loses nothing: the infinite light of the Essence is still there and unchanged, and "you can't not see G-d"; you just don't appreciate what you're seeing, like the cow on the eye doctor's card. That light is not even a *makif* on our world: it is like a person's taste, so the world expresses G-d but cannot define Him.

The *reshimu* is the power of the unlimited to limit itself, but it means that everything was removed, like a footprint. Truer likenesses are the craftsman's notes, the mnemonic, the thrown stone and the peace sign: the world looks like a system running on its own. Yet everything comes out of the *reshimu* through the *Kav*, as a house from its blueprint. G-d does not need a blueprint; He makes the world look fixed so that the *avoda* is ours. The purpose of man is to see past the first *tzimtzum*.

terms.gloss: the empty place: the first tzimtzum, which allows something that appears separate from G-d to exist
shortening: the teacher teaching in short, the Mishna that holds the Gemara
the impression left after the tzimtzum: everything is removed, and yet it includes everything in a hidden way
the line, the ray of light through which G-d reveals the hishtalshelus out of the reshimu
an encompassing light on something inner, already defined by what it surrounds, like a wish for ice cream or a person's house
the power of limitation in the unlimited Or Ein Sof: to reveal the whole infinite light in a limited way
an impression, an outline: the craftsman's blueprint or personal notes
the power once it is thrown and separate from the one who threw it, as against plain Malchus, the hand moving the thing
what is formed; all that is formed is not missing from You
a point; the reshimu as a point holds two opposites, concealment and revelation
a born light: an induced light, like the glow of metal heated by a light behind it; the Kav
literally; the tzimtzum is not literal from G-d's point of view

sections.title: The empty place: G-d hides His light, but it is still there, unchanged
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* hides G-d's essential light so that something that seems separate from Him can exist and the light can later be revealed in it. But like the teacher who teaches in short, nothing is lost: the infinite light is still there, the darkness is only from our side, and what the *Kav* reveals is the very light that was before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.en: the *nimshal* for everything that we said in chapter 12 about the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*,

phrases.he: יובן למעלה בכללות ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי,
phrases.en: is understood in G-dliness about the *tzimtzum* that's called the *makom panui*; the *tzimtzum* is called the empty place.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת הסתלקות וההעלם לעצמותו כדי שיוכל להיות אחר כך בחינת השפעת אור כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This idea of this *tzimtzum* is that G-d hides His essential light in order to be able to later bring it in and reveal it, so that it should be able to be in our world.

blocks.text: The *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of chapter 12's *tzimtzum* (contraction) and *reshimu* (the impression left after it) is the *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* (the empty place), a place to put something: room for our world, which appears separate from G-d. He hides His essential light **in order to be able to later bring it in and reveal it** in our world.

phrases.en: But it's not that it's completely hidden.

phrases.he: אלא כמשל הסתלקות והעלם בעצמו, הידיעה של כל העומק והאריכות כששונה דרך קיצור כנ"ל
phrases.en: G-d's light is not completely hidden; it's like a teacher that when he's explaining it simply, he doesn't forget everything that he knew.

blocks.text: Like the teacher who puts aside the deep explanation and feeds it to the student slowly. **But it's not that it's completely hidden:** a teacher explaining simply does not forget what he knew, and neither is G-d's light gone.
So when G-d creates a table, G-d does not become a table. He does not lose His ability by dealing with our world.

phrases.en: If so,

phrases.he: גם אחר כל ההשתלשלות דאבי''ע שעומד במקום פנוי זה,
phrases.en: even after the whole *hishtalshelus* to create the four worlds that stand in this empty place,

phrases.he: הרי בחינת העלם אור העצמות מקיף וסובב לכל השתלשלות דקו
phrases.en: the essence, the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, G-d's essential self-revelation, which means the revelation of G-d exactly the way He is, is still there.

phrases.he: וכמו שהיה אור העצמות קודם הצמצום ממלא את כל החלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הזה
phrases.en: And just like the light of G-d's essence, the revelation of G-d, before the *tzimtzum* filled this place,
so too after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: הרי ישנו לאור העצמיות כמו שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: G-d's light is still completely infinite; there's still a completely infinite revelation of G-d exactly the way He is,

phrases.he: רק שלא נגלה למטה לגבי שפע המקבלים
phrases.en: just that we're not seeing.

phrases.he: אבל לגבי עצמותו אין שינוי בזה כלל
phrases.en: But G-d still sees everything else, and there's no change to Him.

phrases.he: וכמו משל היודע כל האריכות להשיב לשואלו מיד, גם בשעה ששונה לתלמידו בקיצור כו'.
phrases.en: Like somebody that knows the whole *pilpul* of the Gemara: even when he's explaining it simply, in short, if you ask him a question, he'll right away tell you the whole thing.

blocks.text: **If so, even after the whole hishtalshelus** (the chain of descent) of the four worlds in this empty place, the *Atzmus Ein Sof* (G-d's essence), G-d revealed exactly as He is, **is still there.**
It is only hidden from us. People ask whether you can see G-d; really, "you can't not see G-d." Whatever you experience, you are experiencing the *Atzmus Ein Sof*; you just don't appreciate it.

As the light of the Essence filled this place before the *tzimtzum*, as *Etz Chaim* says, **so too after the tzimtzum** it is completely infinite, G-d as He is, **just that we're not seeing.** G-d still knows all He could do.

Choosing this one world and these ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) does not mean He couldn't make another, or use thirty, or things that are not *sefiros* at all. There are infinite *sefiros* and worlds, all still revealed to Him; to us He revealed one possibility.

**But G-d still sees everything else, and there's no change to Him**, like a scholar who explains the *pilpul* (Talmudic debate) in short and, asked, tells you all of it at once. So if we *daven* (pray), G-d could reveal at once whatever we need, or everything.

phrases.en: This that it says, this is *Tehillim* chapter 19, that G-d makes darkness His concealment,
like it says in the Gemara,
at the beginning there's darkness and afterwards there's light.
This darkness is only for us, but not to G-d.

phrases.he: שנמשך רק מבחינת הרשימו שנשאר אחר ההעלם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: For us we only get the light out of the *reshimu*, which is darkness, and we have to pull out the light.

blocks.text: **G-d makes darkness His concealment** (*Tehillim* chapter 19, as he gives it). The Gemara says goats, usually black, run ahead of the white lambs: **at the beginning there's darkness and afterwards there's light.**

blocks.question: Why does evil start out on the top, and only afterwards is there good?
blocks.text: This is how G-d made the world: first a *tzimtzum* and darkness, and only then He reveals the light.

blocks.title: The puzzle
blocks.text: Our world is like a puzzle: the answer is hidden and looks impossible until you think in a new way and pull it out. Everything around us reveals G-d, but looks hidden, and we must pull it out.
**This darkness is only for us, but not to G-d**, who sees the solution. We get the light only from the *reshimu*, which is darkness, and must pull it out.

phrases.he: וזהו אתה קדוש ושמך, אור העצמי, קדוש ומובדל
phrases.en: This is what it means that You are holy and Your name is holy.
that You are He before He created the world, and You are He after He created the world.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי כו'
phrases.en: I am G-d, I do not change.
why is it the same?
this that G-d reveals deep things from the darkness,
and the concealment,
out from this *reshimu*, out from this concealment, G-d reveals the *hishtalshelus* to us in the *Kav*,

phrases.he: הוא דווקא מאותו אור העצמות שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: That revelation is really the original light from before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: **You are holy and Your name is holy:** G-d's essence stays above the whole *hishtalshelus*, and even His name, His light, stays holy and removed, untouched by the *tzimtzum*. From His point of view the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal).

**You are He before He created the world, and You are He after He created the world.** *Ata* (you), second person, is revelation; *hu* (he), third person, concealment. His essence is revealed the same before and after the *tzimtzum*.

The revelation we see in the world reveals His essence just as the infinite light before the *tzimtzum* did: **I am G-d, I do not change.** The *Ani* (I) is also *Malchus* (kingship), the revelation. We see it as different, but it is the same revelation of Him.
Why the same? What G-d reveals **from the darkness**, the *hishtalshelus* shining in the *Kav* (the ray of light) out of the *reshimu*, is the very light of the Essence from before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.title: The Gemara pulled out of the Mishna
blocks.text: **That revelation is really the original light from before the tzimtzum**, like the Gemara reconstituted from the Mishna, which was set up for that: the same Gemara, the original *sechel* (intellect). So the G-dliness we find in the world is the light from before the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: Not a makif on a pnimi: the Essence is not defined by our world
sections.summary: The light of the Essence around the chain is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*, the way the general *makif* of the *Kav* surrounds the four worlds; it is not even in the category of a light that is given. Like a person's taste, it affects everything without relating to any one thing: our world expresses G-d, but G-d cannot be defined by our world.

phrases.he: ואמנם לא נקרא אור העצמות שמקיף ההשתלשלות שבמקום פנוי כו', כמו בחינת מקיף לפנימי,
phrases.en: But nevertheless, even though the light that comes out in our *hishtalshelus* is coming from the revelation of G-d, we don't say that the light of G-d's essence is like a *makif* for the *hishtalshelus* in a way of *makif l'pnimi*.

phrases.he: כמקיף הכללי דקו שמקיף לאבי''ע בשוה כו'
phrases.en: unlike the general *makif* of the *Kav*, which surrounds *ABYA* equally, which is a *makif* on the *pnimi*.

blocks.text: Yet the light of the Essence is not a *makif* (encompassing light) of the *hishtalshelus* in the way of a *makif l'pnimi*, a *makif* on something inner.

blocks.title: Ice cream, a light bulb, a movie camera
blocks.text: A *makif l'pnimi*, explained later, is like the desire for ice cream: general, including every step to get it, yet tied to a goal and defined by it. Or a light bulb, built to give light; or a movie camera, its lens made transparent for a purpose.

blocks.title: A person's taste
blocks.text: Here it is like a person's taste. It affects everything he does, the flavor and the cone, his house down to the bathroom drapes, yet relates to no one detail more than another.

blocks.title: The house and the sky
blocks.text: It surrounds and truly causes without relating directly. A person's house is a *makif* on a *pnimi*: built for him, controlled by him, defined by him. The sky is not: it does not relate to you; if it is going to rain, it rains.

This *makif* not on a *pnimi* means G-d can be revealed in anything, not specifically our world. The light before the *tzimtzum* is not His ability to make this world but Him as He is, a *hiyuli* (raw potential) that can also come out as our world. It works one way: our world does not define G-d, yet expresses Him, since His light is *makif* on it.

It is **unlike the general makif of the Kav**, surrounding *ABYA* (the four worlds) equally, a *makif* on the *pnimi*: *sovev kol almin* (the light that encompasses all worlds), G-dliness as it relates to our world, the ten *sefiros*, the Creator. The Essence does not relate specifically to our world.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 31 opens by finishing line 14, which class 30 read at its end.

phrases.he: כי הרי עדיין אינו בגדר וסוג בחינת אור השפעה כלל,
phrases.en: because the essence, the light before the *tzimtzum*, G-d's self-revelation, doesn't relate at all to be something to be given over.

phrases.he: גם לא להיות בחינת מקיף כו'
phrases.en: You can't even call it like a general thing, like a *makif*.

phrases.he: רק אור העצמות, שהוא בחינת התגלותו כמו שהוא בעצמות
phrases.en: The light is just a revelation of G-d exactly as He is.

blocks.text: The Essence has nothing to do with being given over, as the power of movement holds no particular movements, being outside the realm of movement. **You can't even call it like a general thing, like a makif.**
It is **just a revelation of G-d exactly as He is**, as with the *hiyuli*: not coats, not shoes, not a power of movement, just Him.

phrases.en: therefore we say,
He endures
and His name endures,
yet we also say, blessed be He and blessed be His name.

phrases.he: רק מבחינת אותיות דגליף בטהירו עילאה זה,
phrases.en: The revelation of our world is coming only from what G-d estimated in the *tehiru ila'a*, in the *glif glifu*, in *Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא מה ששיער בעצמו בכח כו'
phrases.en: which is what G-d estimated in potential, how He wants it to be.

phrases.he: וגם זה הוא הנשאר בבחינת העלם והסתלקות קצת
phrases.en: But even this estimation, even that that was estimated, the *tzimtzum* also hid that,

phrases.he: דהיינו רק לפי ערך אופן הנצרך להשתלשלות אחר צמצום זה
phrases.en: and it's only revealed according to what is needed for this *tzimtzum*, but it's not fully revealed,

blocks.text:
So we say **He endures and His name endures**: they are still found after the *tzimtzum*; and **blessed be He and blessed be His name**: His essence is revealed in our *hishtalshelus*.

But our world's revelation comes only from what G-d estimated in potential in the *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity), the *glif glifu* (the engraving), *Kadmon*: like taste, explained later, which shapes every detail without being estimated for one.
**But even this estimation** the *tzimtzum* hid; it is **only revealed according to what is needed for this tzimtzum**, not fully, *v'dai l'mevin* (enough for one who understands).

That was the *nimshal* of the teacher. As the teacher does not forget, G-d lost nothing; He has no identity crisis on becoming a table. As the teacher sees the whole Gemara in the Mishna, G-d sees His essence fully revealed in the world.

Study anything in the world, a table, a pear, and you will find G-d there, the whole infinite Essence. Because of the *reshimu* it looks hidden, but we can work to pull out the light until we reach the original light: we don't appreciate what we're seeing, but we are seeing it.

blocks.title: The eye doctor's card
blocks.text: Rabbi Walters used to go on *mivtzaim* (outreach) with an eye doctor whose business card had a black and white picture on the back: "What am I?" You see nothing. He turns it the right way up; still nothing. It's a cow, he says; you squint and see no cow, until he points out the eye, the ear, the nose, the body, the fence, and it clicks: a photograph of a cow in a field. Once it clicks, you see the cow every time, for the rest of your life.

So with the world: you see G-d the whole time; it just does not click. The Torah, the *mitzvos*, *Chassidus*, the *birur* (refinement) of the sparks, put it in order; see how it all fits and it clicks: you are looking at G-d.

sections.title: The soul and the body: connected, yet not changed
sections.summary: By the second *mashal*, the soul's life in the body: the soul is bound to the body and affected by it, yet it loses nothing when a limb fails. So the light of the Essence shines after the *tzimtzum*, connected to the measured revelation of the *Kav*, and is not changed by it. All the *meshalim* come to one point.

phrases.he: וגם על פי אופן משל הב' הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: also according to the second *mashal*,
the consciousness of the soul that's in the body,

phrases.he: שמשתנה ממהות רוחני למהות גשמי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that it changes from being spiritual in nature and essence to being physical,

phrases.he: גם כן אין זה שינוי כלל,
phrases.en: This is also not a real change,

phrases.he: שהרי כמו שיש קישור וחיבור לחיות הגשמי לחיות הרוחני
phrases.en: just like there is a bond and a connection between the physical consciousness and the spiritual consciousness,

phrases.he: ממה שרואים התפעלות הנפש ממקרי חיות הגוף,
phrases.en: like we see that the soul is affected by what happens to the body.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה לא ישתנה בעצם הרוחנית מחסרון התפשטות חיות אבר גשמי כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: And on the other hand, it's not affected if something happens to the physical body.

phrases.he: כך אין שינוי בבחינת אור העצמות, להיותו מאיר גם אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: So too, even when G-d shines, reveals Himself after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: גם שאינו רק לפי ערך ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: and even though after the *tzimtzum* G-d reveals Himself in a way of *memalei*, individualized according to the proportion and the relationship of the *hishtalshelus*,
nevertheless, even though it's being revealed in a limited way after the *tzimtzum*, it's still connected to the *Atzmus* of the light before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בצמצום האור בבחינת הקו,
phrases.en: even though it comes in a measured way,

phrases.he: אין זה שינוי כלל באור העצמות על פי משל זה
phrases.en: So there's no real change in the light of the *Atzmus*, based on this *mashal*.

blocks.text: After the *nimshal* of the first *mashal*, the teacher, comes the second, the soul and the body: **the consciousness of the soul that's in the body**, which **changes from being spiritual in nature and essence to being physical**.

**This is also not a real change**: creating the world changes nothing in G-d. There is **a bond and a connection between the physical consciousness and the spiritual consciousness**: what perceives in the body, and gets happy and sad, is the soul, so the soul is affected by the body.

The soul's essence connects to the body, revealed in it not fully. **And on the other hand, it's not affected if something happens to the physical body**: if the eye is ruined, G-d forbid, the soul keeps its sight. So this table reveals G-d, but burning it does not hurt G-d.

After the *tzimtzum* G-d is revealed as *memalei* (filling), measured to the *hishtalshelus*, yet connected to the Essence. In measure there is *hispaalus* (being affected), so to speak: He answers prayers, something holy reveals Him more, the revelation can leave, measure for measure. That is only after. **So there's no real change in the light of the Atzmus, based on this mashal.**

phrases.he: וכן על פי משל הג' מכח התנועה בגשם או כמשל התחכמות מכח המשכיל הנזכר לעיל

phrases.en: it all comes up to one general point,

blocks.text: By the third *mashal* too, movement in the body or intellect in the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight), **it all comes up to one general point.** Making the world does not lessen G-d, who sees in it His full revelation; it is there for us too, unappreciated. G-d Himself answers prayer, with no change.

sections.title: The reshimu is the power of limitation in the unlimited light
sections.summary: The *reshimu*, compared above to the short version that includes the whole length, is in G-dliness the *koach hahagbala*: the power of the unlimited light to bring all of itself, limited, into one impression, even into a speck of dust. G-d can do anything, and so He can also limit.

phrases.en: the *reshimu* that was explained previously,

phrases.he: שזהו כמו הקיצור שכלול בו כל האריכות
phrases.en: which is like the summary that includes the whole *arichus*, like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara,

phrases.he: הנה למעלה יובן מזה שזהו בחינת כח ההגבלה שיש באור אין סוף הבלתי מוגבל בעצם
phrases.en: But *reshimu* in the *nimshal* is the power of limitation that exists in the *Or Ein Sof*, which is essentially not limited.

phrases.he: דהיינו להביא כל הארות אור העצמות הבלתי גבול בבחינת הגבול
phrases.en: In other words, the power of the light is to reveal G-d; the power of the *reshimu* is to reveal G-d in a limited way.
that's the idea of the impression,

phrases.he: שכולל בבחינת הגבלה מבחינת כל עצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: that it includes in a limited way the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*,
like the *kitzur* that includes everything, like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara.

blocks.text: Now the *nimshal* for the *reshimu*: **the reshimu that was explained previously**, the summary that includes the whole length, **like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara**.

In the *nimshal* the *reshimu* is the power of limitation in the unlimited *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light). **The power of the light is to reveal G-d; the power of the reshimu is to reveal G-d in a limited way**: the whole *gilui* (revelation) of the Essence in an infinitely little speck of dust on this table.

**That's the idea of the impression**: it holds the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, limited, as the *kitzur* (shortening) holds everything, the Mishna the Gemara. G-d packs the whole Essence into the smallest thing; study even the tiniest particle properly and you would find it there.

phrases.en: because G-d can do anything; He's omnipotent,

phrases.he: וכלול בו גם כן מכח המגביל
phrases.en: He also has the power to limit.

phrases.he: להגביל ולכלול ברשימה א' מכל אור העצמות כו'
phrases.en: So He also has the power to limit and to include in a single impression, in a single point, all the light of the *Atzmus*.

blocks.text: **Because G-d can do anything; He's omnipotent,** He can also limit, and does it well: all the infinite light of the *Atzmus* revealed infinitesimally, in a single impression, a single point, as explained elsewhere. That is the main *nimshal*.
But the Mishna, the *kitzur*, is not a good *mashal* for the *reshimu*: the other *meshalim* (analogies) will show it is more limited still, not only very dense.

sections.title: Truer likenesses: the craftsman's mark, the mnemonic, the thrown stone, the hint
sections.summary: The *reshimu* means that everything was taken away, like a footprint when the foot is gone, so the short version is not a true likeness. Truer are the craftsman's line, the mnemonic, and most of all the thrown stone, whose force is hidden in it and in the arm, and the hand's sign or the writing that hides an idea: the world looks separate and self-running, and G-d's involvement is hidden in it.

phrases.he: אך הנה באמת אין זה דמיון אמיתי לבחינת הרשימו הנשאר בחלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This *mashal*, this comparison to the *kitzur*, is not the proper comparison for the *reshimu* that's left over in this empty place.

phrases.he: כי הוא מורה שנסתלק משם הכל
phrases.en: because the idea of the *reshimu* indicates that everything was removed; that doesn't mean that it was just made very condensed, it means that it's not there.

phrases.he: ולא שנשאר איזה אור רק שהוא בקצור וגבול,
phrases.en: and not that there was some light left, there's a little bit of a revelation, it's just very condensed,

phrases.he: אלא רק בחינת רשימו בעלמא כו'
phrases.en: but only an impression, meaning that the original thing was taken away, like a footprint; the foot's gone.

blocks.text: The *kitzur* is not the true comparison for the *reshimu* in the empty place: a *reshimu* means everything was removed, not some light left condensed, only an impression. Like a footprint: **the foot's gone.**

phrases.he: אם כן הדמיון האמיתי הוא מרושם וציון קו קצר שעושין האומנין, שכולל כל אריכות מעשה הבנין
phrases.en: So if so, a better *mashal* is like the little blueprint or the little notes that a craftsman makes for how to build the entire thing,
even more than this,
like a mnemonic,
so too in G-dliness,

phrases.he: כתיב זכר רב טובך, העצמי כו'
phrases.en: that our world is only like a *zecher*, is only like a remembrance of G-d's abundant goodness.
and the like.

blocks.title: The craftsman's notes
blocks.text: The true likeness is **the little blueprint or the little notes that a craftsman makes for how to build the entire thing**: unlike the Mishna it explains nothing, only a line, yet from it he builds everything.
**Even more than this**, a mnemonic, completely hidden. **So too in G-dliness**: "Remember Your abundant goodness"; our world is only a remembrance of it, the letters of a mnemonic, **and the like.**

The *reshimu* means G-d's light is completely hidden in the world, which is why a person naturally feels he sees a physical world, not G-d. It hints at Him like a mnemonic or a blueprint, a foreign thing: a table, being created, hints at a Creator, but we see the hint, not the Creator.

phrases.he: ויותר בהעלם והסתלקות הוא כמשל הזורק אבן כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Or even more so is like the *mashal* of throwing a stone, which is the main *mashal* of the *reshimu*.
like it says in *Sefer HaBahir*,
like it was thrown.

phrases.he: שהרי בחינת הרשימו נשאר נבדל בריחוק מקום מעצמות האור וכו'
phrases.en: because the *reshimu* is left so that it seems like it's distant from the *Atzmus HaOr*,
And the power that's hidden within this *reshimu* is called

phrases.he: בחינת העלם אור, נבדל מהעלם עצמות האור דאין סוף
phrases.en: the concealment of the light, which is separate from the essential concealment of the light of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: כמו כח נבדל הנעלם בזריקת אבן
phrases.en: Like when you throw a stone: there's a power of movement, there's a force that's hidden now within the stone,

phrases.he: שבא מכח היד שכבר נעלם בעצמו כו'
phrases.en: And also in the person's arm that threw it, you don't see the implementation of his force.

blocks.text: **Or even more so**, it is like throwing a stone, the main *mashal* of the *reshimu*; *Sefer HaBahir* says **like it was thrown.** The *reshimu* seems far from the Essence, and our world looks thrown: we hardly see G-d's involvement.

Not that it is so, but the world can look thrown, as if G-d made it once and it runs on its own, a big bang that sent everything flying. A natural system looks independent, as if it had left G-dliness altogether.

The power hidden in this *reshimu* is **the concealment of the light, which is separate from the essential concealment of the light of the Ein Sof.** In a thrown stone the hand's force is hidden; you see only that it moves. **And also in the person's arm that threw it, you don't see the implementation of his force**: the arm is at rest.

Why "separate from the concealment of the Essence"? Because it is hidden twice, as in the stone and the arm: within the world, and G-d's involvement too. Without miracles we don't see His hand, so to speak; He seems to sit back while the world goes on its own. That is the main thing of the *tzimtzum*: G-d looks uninvolved, and we feel independent of Him.

phrases.en: like all the orbits and stars, or the planets and the stars,
that are moving from G-d's power of movement,

phrases.he: הנעלם, שבא בבחינת זריקה מאור וכח האלה״י
phrases.en: which is hidden within them, from G-d's power of throwing,
the *chitzoniyus* nine *kelim* of *Malchus d'Asiya*,

phrases.he: שנקרא זה כח הנבדל בחינת מלכות שבמלכות
phrases.en: once they're actually thrown, that is called *Malchus sheb'Malchus*,
which *Malchus sheb'Malchus* is where it becomes far from you,

phrases.he: ולא כמו הכתיבה באצבע או כח יד הפועל עצמו בנפעל
phrases.en: and not like when you're writing or when you're moving something with your hand,
when you're actually moving something directly with your hand, that's the revelation of your power in a way that's close, that you see the connection.
That's just plain *Malchus*.

blocks.text: So the *galgalim* (celestial orbits), planets and stars, are moved by G-d's power of throwing hidden in them: **the chitzoniyus nine kelim** (the outer nine vessels) **of Malchus d'Asiya**, which set the universe moving; the nine planets match them.

Once thrown, that separate power is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*. Holding something and moving it, the power still connected, is plain *Malchus*, its first nine *sefiros*; throwing it, separate from you, is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*.

All these levels exist; it depends on what you perceive. Seeing that every moment G-d moves the planets is the nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*. Seeing them as thrown, maybe by G-d once, but running on since the Big Bang, is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*.

That is the *reshimu*: G-d's involvement is hidden, but since He did it you can find a hint of Him, like graphology. *Malchus sheb'Malchus* **is where it becomes far from you**; moving something with your hand, where you see the connection, **That's just plain Malchus.** He notes that a parenthesis here seems misplaced.

phrases.en: and *meshalim* that are even closer for this, the idea of the *reshimu*,
like a hint with a hand motion for a *sechel*.
The movement lifting those two fingers hints at a whole thing, but the *sechel* is completely hidden there.

phrases.he: שזהו נקרא בחינת הלבשה ותפיסא בדבר נבדל כו'
phrases.en: That is the idea that it changes its *mahus*: it's being represented by something, it's enclothed in something different, and it's being expressed by that.

phrases.he: וכן כשכותב שכל וחכמה בתנועת האצבע כו'
phrases.en: Same thing when you're writing: there the intellect goes through the hand, and it's hidden, but then it comes out through being on paper.

blocks.title: The peace sign
blocks.text: Closer still: **a hint with a hand motion for a sechel**, like the peace sign. Lifting two fingers hints at a whole thing, but the *sechel* is completely hidden; a person sees a movement, not intellect.

So we see only a physical world, no meaning, because we don't know the language. We see fingers; in the *nimshal*, trees, tables, sky. Whoever says he does not see G-d does not understand what these symbols represent.
This is called being enclothed and grasped in a separate thing: **it changes its mahus** (what a thing is in itself). It is enclothed in something different and expressed by it.

blocks.title: G-d writing His autobiography
blocks.text: **Same thing when you're writing**: the intellect passes hidden through the hand and comes out on paper. The world is a language: G-d is writing, "as He's writing His autobiography," and the world's changes are the changes on the paper.

That is how revelation comes out of the *reshimu* again. The *reshimu* is the written thing, the hand's movement, with the intellect completely hidden in it. Take the world at face value, each thing separate and unconnected, and you see no meaning. See how it all fits together, as the next chapter explains, and it is a language, though no single letter on the paper means anything.

phrases.he: כך למעלה, בחינת הרשימו בחינת דבר נבדל בערך,
phrases.en: so too, *reshimu* is the idea that reality seems like something that's separate from G-dliness.

phrases.he: שבו מלובש בהעלם מכללות אור העצמות כו'
phrases.en: but nevertheless, really the whole light of G-d is hidden within our world, and if we'll look into it, we'll be able to find it.

blocks.text: So too above, **reality seems like something that's separate from G-dliness**: the table is not G-d, it is a table. That is the whole root of *avoda zara* (idol worship): this is a world, not G-d.

And His involvement is hidden too: He is revealed through something that seems separate, and the *mahus* changes from infinite to physical and limited. **But nevertheless, really the whole light of G-d is hidden within our world, and if we'll look into it, we'll be able to find it.**

sections.title: Everything comes from the reshimu: nothing is missing from You
sections.summary: Though everything was removed and the light remains in the *reshimu* only hidden, short and hinted, or as a thrown, separate power, all the details of the *Kav* come from it, because it includes everything. It holds what G-d estimated in *Kadmon*, seen in one glance; so all that is formed is not missing "from You".

phrases.en: however, from all of these *meshalim* together,

phrases.he: יובן על כל פנים כללות ענין הרשימו
phrases.en: it's at least understood, the general *inyan* of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: דגם שהוא בא בבחינת הסתלקות הכל,
phrases.en: that even though the *reshimu* comes in a way where everything is removed,

phrases.he: ולא נשאר בה רק בהעלם גדול
phrases.en: the original light only remains in the *reshimu* in a very hidden way,
it's completely short and just hinted at,
or it can also be looked at in a little bit different way: it's like something that was thrown, that it's now seen as something that's separate and outside from the self.
nevertheless,

phrases.he: מזה עצמו בא ונמשך כל פרטי ההשתלשלות דקו
phrases.en: from this itself, from this *reshimu* itself, comes all the details of what comes on into the *Kav*, through the *Kav*.
it all comes from this *reshimu*.
because in this little impression,

phrases.he: להיותה כוללת הכל בהעלם על כל פנים,
phrases.en: since it includes everything, albeit in a very hidden way,

phrases.he: היא הנותנת שיוכל לבא הכל בהתגלות על ידי בחינת הקו
phrases.en: this is what gives the possibility that everything should be able to come out from it, should be revealed from it through the *Kav*,
everything in *hishtalshelus* until the end of *Asiya*, the physical world.

blocks.text: Having given each *mashal*'s *nimshal*, now the general idea: **it's at least understood, the general inyan** (concept) of the *reshimu*. Everything is removed, the original light remains very hidden, **it's completely short and just hinted at**; or, seen differently, it is something thrown, now separate, outside the self.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 33 opens by summing up the meshalim of lines 34-53 before it reads line 54.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless**, hidden and short as the light is in it, from this *reshimu* come all the details of what comes through the *Kav*: **it all comes from this reshimu.**

Because this little impression includes everything, however hidden, it lets everything come out and be revealed through the *Kav*. Once it is there, the *Kav* can pull it back out; how, when that seems very hard or impossible, the next chapter explains.

Were it not there at all, it would be *tzimtzum kipshuto*, hidden for good. Mainly it holds what *Kadmon* estimated for the *hishtalshelus* (other *sefiros* are hidden there too and do not come out, though they could); deeper, the whole light of the Essence, from which anything can be drawn: **everything in hishtalshelus until the end of Asiya, the physical world.**

phrases.he: וכמאמר כל היצור לא נכחד ממך
phrases.en: like it says that all of what is created, or really *yetzur* means what is formed, is not missing from You.
from You, *davka*, meaning from G-d Himself.

phrases.he: שזהו הכל נעשה ונמשך בגלוי כמו שעלה ברצונו הפשוט בעצמות האור שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: that everything in the *hishtalshelus* is done according to, is made and is brought out according to the way that it arose in G-d's simple will within Himself,
in the estimation that He made in the light before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שהרי במחשבה קדומה זו ששיער בעצמו
phrases.en: because in this original thought where He estimated it to Himself, and this we mean *Kadmon* here,

phrases.he: הוא צופה ומביט הכל בסקירה א'
phrases.en: He saw everything from the beginning to the end in one glance.

phrases.he: דהיינו מה שנסקר בהעלם ובקיצור ורמז ברשימו זו כו'
phrases.en: And this whole estimation is what's put into this impression, this *reshimu*, and in this *reshimu*, everything is seen in a hidden and in a very short and hinted way, in one glance.

blocks.text: As it says, all that is formed (*yetzur*) is not missing from You. **From You, davka** (specifically): everything in the world comes from G-d Himself.

Everything in the *hishtalshelus* comes out as it arose in G-d's simple will, **in the estimation that He made in the light before the tzimtzum**: in that original thought, *Kadmon*, **He saw everything from the beginning to the end in one glance.**
This whole estimation is put into the *reshimu*, where everything is seen hidden, very short and hinted, in one glance: like one point, with everything hidden in it.

sections.title: The craftsman's blueprint: a plan kept so that the work is ours
sections.summary: The craftsman builds the whole house from his outline, which he makes so that he will not deviate or have to think it through again. G-d does not forget; turning the *mashal* around, He makes the world look like a fixed system He set up once, so that the *avoda* falls on us and we feel the responsibility.

phrases.en: and this is like the analogy of the craftsman's blueprint,

phrases.he: שממנו דוקא ידע לעשות כל אריכות מעשה הבנין בפרטי פרטיו
phrases.en: that specifically from looking at the blueprint, the craftsman knows how to make everything: he can build the whole house from the blueprint, with all of its most minute details,
from its beginning to its end.

phrases.he: רק כדי שלא יתעלם ממנו טעמו ונימוקו בעצמותו לאריכות הענין, הוא עושה לו רושם לזכרון
phrases.en: He makes it so that he will not forget the whole reason of why he decided to do it exactly this way.
so that he shouldn't deviate from it,
and he won't have to go think about it again.

blocks.title: The craftsman's blueprint
blocks.text: It is like **the analogy of the craftsman's blueprint**: specifically from the blueprint, the craftsman knows how to build the whole house in its most minute details, **from its beginning to its end.**

Why make one? Only its maker fully understands a blueprint, especially when it is no standard one: a craftsman's *roshem* (outline) can be personal notes. **He makes it so that he will not forget the whole reason of why he decided to do it exactly this way**, once he is in the middle of building.

**So that he shouldn't deviate from it, and he won't have to go think about it again.** Mid-building he forgets why he put something here; there seems better, and he must rethink why it won't work structurally, or remember the plumbing has to run that way.

Someone who wants to be an architect told Rabbi Walters they study plumbing and electricity besides engineering, to take it all into account. But while building, he wants to think only about how to build.

phrases.he: וכמו כן ענין הציונים ללימוד עמוק שבעצמו כו'
phrases.en: so too the idea of making little notes, sort of mnemonics, to help you remember a deep subject,

phrases.he: שזהו תועלת לידע מהם כל אורך עיון עומק עצמותו שיש לו, פן ינטה ממנו כו'
phrases.en: and from remembering that, it will remind you the whole *halacha* with all the reasons and everything, and you won't deviate from it.

blocks.title: Notes for a deep subject
blocks.text: **So too the idea of making little notes, sort of mnemonics, to help you remember a deep subject**: after a whole *pilpul* to reach the *halacha* (the law), a short line, like a Mishna or shorter, brings it all back with its reasons, **and you won't deviate from it.**

The *nimshal*: in *Kadmon* G-d estimated everything that will be in the world, down to the hairs on each head, the feathers on every bird, how often every blade of grass shakes in the wind. It must all be exactly so for *Moshiach* to come; that is part of *hashgacha pratis* (divine providence): G-d likes it this way. Now it only brings out what the blueprint planned.

blocks.question: Why would the *mashal* of the blueprint apply to G-d, who is not going to forget or deviate? Why would He need the *reshimu*?
blocks.text: Going from *mashal* to *nimshal* you always adjust. The craftsman's blueprint is so as not to rethink and not to deviate; G-d will neither forget nor err. Of course He needs no *reshimu*: switch it around and put the *mashal*'s deficiencies on us. G-d wants the world to look as if it runs on its own, without His constant involvement.

He wants it to look like a one-time involvement: all figured out, now running. Down to *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) you see Him involved, but only following His system, reaching nothing new from His essence. So He seems neither to go back into the *omek* (depth) nor to deviate: a system.
He wants these two things in order to put the *avoda* (divine service) on us: so that we feel G-d set up the world a certain way.

blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab's oath
blocks.text: They tell that the Rebbe Rashab made G-d swear not to change the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds) when *bochurim* (yeshiva students) get it wrong, so they would work to understand it right: the *reshimu*'s "lest he deviate from it."

G-d commits Himself, so to speak, to run the world a certain way. That gives us our *avoda*: it matters that we do things *davka* this way, for He wants *Moshiach* to come like this and will not let us off. That is what makes it hard.
It should also look as if it no longer comes every moment from His *etzem* (essence); otherwise it would look not like a system but like Him deciding each moment.

blocks.title: The teacher's class plan
blocks.text: Like a teacher who plans a system beforehand, reward and punishment, grades, requirements you must meet to pass, and makes it look like something outside him that he only works within. Otherwise no one feels the weight: he does as he likes, so ask him to be nice and change it.
When we *daven* we do ask G-d to change it, and sometimes He does. Short of going past this level, the *tzimtzum* makes us do *avoda* and feel responsible.

sections.title: The reshimu as the source of the Kav: the point and the vav
sections.summary: Like the blueprint, the *reshimu* holds the whole light hidden and is the source of everything in the *Kav*, so the whole chain looks like a set system following one plan. It is the point with two opposites, hiding what is above it and revealing everything to those below; the *Kav* drawn from it is the *vav* whose head is a *yud*, narrower than its source.

phrases.he: וכך בחינת הרשימו הזאת הכוללת ברמז ובקיצור מכל אור העצמות הנעלם בה,
phrases.en: So just like the blueprint, so too this *reshimu* includes in it, in a hinted, in a *kitzur* way, the whole light of the *Atzmus*, which is hidden in it.

phrases.he: הוא עצמו המקור לכל ההמשכות דקו וחוט
phrases.en: This *reshimu* itself is the source for everything that comes out in the *Kav*.
both the *makifim* of the *hishtalshelus* and the *pnimi* of the *hishtalshelus*, from its beginning all the way to its end,

phrases.he: שיהיה הכל כמו שעלה ברצונו וחכמתו הפשוטה בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש כו'
phrases.en: that it should all be according to the way that He originally wanted, with His will and His wisdom, simple will and wisdom, in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*.

blocks.text: **So just like the blueprint**, the *reshimu* holds the whole light of the Essence, hinted and short, and **this reshimu itself is the source for everything that comes out in the Kav**: the rest of the *hishtalshelus* comes through this *tzimtzum*, and this step defines it all.
So it looks thrown, a *hishtalshelus* G-d set up that now runs. That is why many see Kabbala as a machine, a system: G-d made it set, and from there down we understand Him through it.

So for the *makifim* (encompassing lights) and the *pnimi* (inner light), **from its beginning all the way to its end**, everything follows the *reshimu*: **it should all be according to the way that He originally wanted**, His simple will and wisdom in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*, a one-time plan.

phrases.en: this is what is explained elsewhere,
that a point, which the *reshimu* is compared to a point, has two aspects to it. It has concealment and revelation,
two opposites, two opposite things.

phrases.he: העלם מכל מה שעליון הימנה בערך,
phrases.en: that the point, the *reshimu*, is a concealment of everything that's higher than it, relative to it.
and it's the source of the revelation of everything to the recipients.
It all comes out from it.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הקו שנמשך מן הרשימו
phrases.en: and the revelation that comes to the recipients is the *Kav* that comes from the *reshimu*,
the relationship of the *Kav* to the *reshimu* is like the letter *vav*;
the head of it is a *yud*, which represents the *reshimu*: it's a point,
and then from that point it's drawn down,
as explained elsewhere at length, how the *Kav* is drawn out from the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, a point (*nekuda*), to which the *reshimu* is compared, holds **two opposites, two opposite things.** It is **a concealment of everything that's higher than it, relative to it**: the whole Essence is in it, too short and hinted to see. **And it's the source of the revelation of everything to the recipients.**

blocks.title: A funnel, and CliffNotes
blocks.text: Like a funnel channeling everything from above. The Mishna, like CliffNotes of the Gemara Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi knew, is for us the source of the whole Gemara.

The *Kav* drawn from the *reshimu* brings the revelation, shaped like a *vav* headed by a *yud*: the *yud*, a point, is the *reshimu*, and the line is drawn down from it, **as explained elsewhere at length, how the Kav is drawn out from the reshimu.**

The *vav*'s line is thinner than the *yud*, which, though a point, has some width: the *Kav* is less than the *reshimu*. The *reshimu* is a point from the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite), a zero, but "the nothing of the *reshimu* is bigger than everything in our *hishtalshelus*."

The *Kav* never brings out all that is hidden in the *reshimu*: the whole Gemara explains the Mishna, and there is still more to pull out forever. The same *roshem* that yields this world could yield totally different worlds, as explained elsewhere.

sections.title: Summing up: G-d limits Himself so that all is revealed, and the purpose of man is to see past it
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav* are G-d limiting Himself, so to speak, so that this world can be revealed; He hid everything else He could do, and the choosing is itself a revelation. From His own light comes a born light, the *Kav*, like a glowing sheet of metal. The whole of man is to feel this deeply and see past the first *tzimtzum*, and so be bound to G-d Himself.

phrases.he: ובכל זה מובן כללות ענין הצמצום דמקום פנוי
phrases.en: From all of this, we understand the general *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui*, the empty place *tzimtzum*,
and the impression that was left,
and also the line which comes out from the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: שהוא רק בחינת הגבלה בעצמות כדי שיומשך הכל בגלוי
phrases.en: That the general idea of the *tzimtzum*, *reshimu*, and the *Kav* is that G-d limits Himself, so to speak, in order that everything should be brought out in a revealed way.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
phrases.en: This is what it says: With You is the source of life,
and from Your light is seen light,
a born light,
which is the idea of the *Kav*.
like will be explained with the help of G-d,

blocks.text: From all this the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui* is understood: to put something in a place you must empty it, so G-d hid Himself, and something could appear separate from Him. **And the impression that was left, and also the line which comes out from the reshimu**, the next two chapters explain.

So *tzimtzum*, *reshimu* and *Kav* mean that **G-d limits Himself, so to speak, in order that everything should be brought out in a revealed way**: to reveal this world, He hid everything else He could do, other worlds, other *sefiros*.
He lost none of His potential, and it is a full revelation of Him, even a greater one: His choosing that it be *davka* this way is itself a *gilui*, and so the *tzimtzum* itself is a *gilui*.

This is **With You is the source of life**; from Your light is seen light. From the light of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, G-d Himself revealed, a different light is seen, *or shel tolda*, **a born light**: the *Kav*, an induced light.

blocks.title: The curtain and the glowing metal
blocks.text: A strong light on a curtain: you see only a new light coming through. Better, a strong light on a sheet of metal no light can pass: it heats the metal, which glows with a new light. The glow shows a light behind it, and where it glows brighter shows where the light is concentrated, but the original you don't see.

Because of the *tzimtzum* we see in the world *chachma* (wisdom) and *middos* (emotional attributes), not G-d Himself. Through *avoda* we go past it and reveal Him: that is why we must work, and make a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). **Like will be explained with the help of G-d**, how the *Kav* works.

phrases.en: and this is the whole purpose of man.
to really become very sensitive for this whole idea, that it should really hit you,
and similar things, meaning the rest of the *hishtalshelus* that we're going to explain the rest of the book,

phrases.he: מפני שמזה דוקא יבוא לכלל היחוד האמיתי בהתקשרות נפשו בחיי כל החיים העליונים, שהוא עצמות אור אין סוף ממש מטעם הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:

blocks.text: This is **the whole purpose of man**: **to really become very sensitive for this whole idea, that it should really hit you**: the whole *hishtalshelus* is nothing, G-d holding back and showing a little of what He can do; see past the first *tzimtzum*.

That is the main purpose of our *avoda*. Even without *mamash* (actually) seeing past it, live with this *daas* (knowledge), so that what you connect to and value is G-d Himself; nothing else should impress you: it is only a means to an end.

With that attitude a person goes with a high hand, unimpressed by the world or even *Gan Eden* (Paradise) and *Olam Haba* (the World to Come), and does his *shlichus* (mission). **And similar things**: the rest of the *hishtalshelus*. See through every *tzimtzum*; this one is in a way the main one.

Only seeing past the concealment G-d set up brings the true union. It makes things look set: there is *teva* (nature), you work within its limits, and so you cannot always do Torah and *mitzvos*; you worry about this and that. Seeing past these limits connects us to G-d: nothing can stop us, and we see what really matters.

Fix both the goal and the way: our *ratzon* (will) only for G-d, and the limits of the *hishtalshelus*, there only to help us connect to Him, cannot stop us. As at the start of chapter 12, understanding this lets you direct your *ratzon* to G-d Himself.

reviewQuestions.question: What does it mean that the light of the Essence is still there after the *tzimtzum*, and why is it impossible not to see G-d?
How is a person's taste different from his wish for ice cream, and what does that show about the light of the Essence and our world?
By the *mashal* of the soul in the body, why is the *tzimtzum* not a change in G-d, even though the light after it is connected to the world?
Why is the short version that includes the whole length not a true likeness for the *reshimu*, and what does the thrown stone add?
G-d will not forget or deviate, so why does the *mashal* of the craftsman's blueprint apply to Him?
What is a "born light", and how do the curtain and the glowing metal explain it?

notes.text: Line 13 ("v'zehu ata hu kulei v'kayadua") is not read in any class; it has a no-recording passage. Class 30 goes from line 12 straight to line 14, though its explanation of line 11 (30 w1117-1313) already covers "ata hu".

Garbled stretches folded into blocks without their unclear words: 31 w1450-1536 ("if something is holy it will reveal G-d more, and if it's the revelation will go away"), rendered as "the revelation can go away"; 33 w1479-1507 ("should not, that should not happen"), left out of the block's text; 30 w363-368 ("It's not there, it's still here"), rendered as "It has not gone somewhere else".

Sensitivity: no block is flagged. Considered and left unflagged: "that's the whole thing of avoda zara" (32 w2109-2132), a Torah point about perceiving the world as separate from G-d that names no group; the remark that Kabbala looks to many people like a machine (34 w133-229), criticism of an impression, not of a group; the eye doctor on mivtzaim and the student who wants to be an architect, both unnamed; and the Rebbe Rashab's oath, a story told about a Rebbe with reverence.

All five tapes have Sofer's word times, not re-timed ones: the seconds can be off; the word ranges are right. The tape titles end in "(N)" (chapter 10's ended in "(M)"); the classes do not say what it stands for.
